title: Core\Markdown::toHtml takes quadratic time over a long run of raw HTML tags that never close.
text: `Core\Str::repeat('<a>', n)` or `'<div>'` costs time in the square of n: 120,000 `<div>` tags take 5.7 s, while `Core\Html::sanitize` over the same text is linear. `rule:core-classes/markdown-cost` promises linear work. Closing it finds the step that rescans the open raw elements per tag (the raw-HTML splice, `groups::Balance`, or the rebuild's passes), makes it linear, and adds a catalogue entry with `work = "linear"` for both inputs.
